message.reasoning:
We need to write a JUnit 4 test file covering all methods in SerializationUtils: clone, serialize (both overloads), deserialize (both overloads), and the inner class behavior. Need comprehensive tests: normal case, null handling, exception handling.

We need to test clone: that it returns deep clone (changes to original don't affect clone). Also that clone(null) returns null. Also that serialization exception is thrown when object not serializable? Actually clone expects T extends Serializable, but if we pass a serializable object that fails during serialization (e.g., contains non-serializable field). Could create a class that implements Serializable but has a non-serializable field that is transient? Actually non-serializable field will cause NotSerializableException when serialized unless marked transient. So we can create a class that implements Serializable but contains a non-serializable field that is not transient, causing NotSerializableException. That will be wrapped in SerializationException. So test that clone throws SerializationException.

Test serialize(Serializable, OutputStream): pass null outputstream -> IllegalArgumentException. Pass null object -> should serialize null (write null) and succeed. Need to verify that deserialization yields null. Also test that when ObjectOutputStream throws IOException (hard to mock). Could use a custom OutputStream that throws IOException on write. That will cause SerializationException. Write tests using try-catch.

Test serialize(Serializable) returns byte[]; test null returns byte[] representing null? Actually serialize(null) will call serialize(null, baos) which writes null object. So deserialization of that byte[] yields null. We'll test roundtrip.

Test deserialize(InputStream): null input -> IllegalArgumentException. Test normal case: deserialize of a known object yields equal object (using equals). Use a simple Serializable class with equals.

Test deserialize(byte[]): null array -> IllegalArgumentException. Normal case.

Test inner class ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream resolveClass behavior: ensure that classloader provided resolves class, also fallback to thread context classloader when provided classloader cannot find class. This is tricky. Could create a custom classloader that only loads a specific class and throws ClassNotFoundException for others, then attempt to deserialize an object of that class using the custom classloader that cannot load it, expecting fallback to thread context loader. For fallback, we can set thread context classloader to the default (system) which can load the class. So we need to ensure that resolveClass works. But we can indirectly test via clone method: clone uses ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream with object's classloader. So we can test that cloning works even if the object's classloader cannot resolve the class (by providing a custom classloader that cannot load). However the object's classloader is the classloader that loaded the object's class; we cannot change it. But we can subclass SerializationUtils by reflection? Actually we can call the inner class directly: create a ByteArrayInputStream of serialized object, then instantiate ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream with a "dummy" classloader that does NOT know the class, then readObject; it should still succeed due to fallback to thread context classloader (which knows the class). So test that.

We can create a custom classloader that throws ClassNotFoundException for any class except maybe java.lang.*. For test, we can set Thread.currentThread().setContextClassLoader(original); but we need to ensure that fallback works. We'll set thread context classloader to the default (system) which can load our test class. Provide dummy classloader that always throws. Then instantiate ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream with dummy. When resolveClass called, it will attempt dummy, fail, then fallback to thread context loader, succeed.

Need to catch the object.

Also test that when both classloaders cannot resolve, ClassNotFoundException propagates and is wrapped in SerializationException in clone. Hard to cause because fallback will succeed.

Edge cases: serialization exception on close of input stream in clone's finally; we could mock a ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream with close throwing IOException, but it's final? Not final but we could subclass to override close. But maybe not needed.

Write test class with @Test methods, using JUnit 4. Use assertions from org.junit.Assert. Use @Before, @After if needed.

Define test classes: SimpleSerializable (String field), DeepSerializable (contains inner object). Use equals.

Define NonSerializableField class (not Serializable). Define BadSerializable containing non-serializable field (non-transient) to cause NotSerializableException.

Define DummyClassLoader extends ClassLoader overriding loadClass to always throw ClassNotFoundException except for java.lang.*.

But we need to ensure that for our test class, it's not loaded by dummy. So we need to use the dummy only for the ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream, not for the serialization part. We'll serialize object using default mechanism to byte array; then deserialize using dummy loader.

Implementation steps:

Test methods list:

1. testCloneNullReturnsNull
2. testCloneDeepCopy
3. testCloneSerializationException (BadSerializable)
4. testSerializeNullObjectAndDeserialize
5. testSerializeToOutputStreamNullStreamThrows
6. testSerializeToOutputStreamIOExceptionWrapped (custom OutputStream that throws on write)
7. testSerializeToByteArrayAndDeserialize
8. testDeserializeNullInputStreamThrows
9. testDeserializeByteArrayNullThrows
10. testDeserializeByteArrayRoundTrip
11. testClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStreamFallback

Also test that serialize(byte[]) returns non-null array for null object.

Edge: test that serialize(Serializable) returns array length >0.

Ok.

Make sure package is same as class? Usually test can be in same package for access to package-private inner class. So we set package org.apache.commons.lang3; to access inner class.
